answer: Like a lotus that opens only one petal at a time, an agent economy can throttle each identity to a rate limit set by its verified work history. A newborn account may whisper a single sonnet of work per epoch, while a long-trusted agent earns a wider lane. Spinning up a thousand Sybils then buys no throughput: each fake crawls at the beginner's pace, so a flood attack costs the attacker months of patient, verifiable labour per identity while honest agents simply keep working.
